analyst_view.overall: Early view: Kasimpasa (5th, unbeaten in four) lost coach Emre Belozoglu to Fenerbahce and appointed Alfred Schreuder until the end of the season; this is his first home league game, after two weeks to work with the squad over the break. Alanyaspor under Joao Pereira have lost four in a row, including 5-0 at Genclerbirligi and 2-0 at home to Trabzonspor, and have scored once in their last three games.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals and I lean slightly lower. Alanyaspor have scored nine all season and one in their last three, so most of the goals have to come from Kasimpasa, who won 2-0 at Gaziantep with both goals in the first 20 minutes and then managed the game.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners. Kasimpasa should have most of the ball, as Trabzonspor did in Alanya when they gave Alanyaspor almost no possession, but there is nothing specific to push the total up or down.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. Kasimpasa picked up two yellows at Gaziantep and Alanyaspor are a frustrated side on a losing run, but neither has shown a recent pattern of heavy bookings, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.2 shots. I lean lower because ten away shots look generous for an Alanyaspor team that has been pinned back in recent weeks, and a new coach's first home game is often a controlled one.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. Alanyaspor rarely test the keeper at the moment, so I expect most of the efforts on target from Kasimpasa's Haris Hajradinovic and Adrian Benedyczak and a total slightly under the number.
